findings.problem: update() is implemented purely as `if (!init(arbiter)) invalidate();` and init() unconditionally sets `_ignored = false` (line 57). So refreshing an existing pair against the same arbiter silently clears the ignore flag: after ignore() is called (which sets the Chipmunk arbiter to the ignore state for the rest of the contact, a state that persists across steps) the next update() makes isIgnored() report false even though Chipmunk is still ignoring the collision. The requirement lists init/update/invalidate as distinct lifecycle steps and ignore/isIgnored as a queryable state, so conflating update with a fresh init loses required state.
findings.fix: Stop delegating the flag reset. Either give update() its own body that re-resolves the shapes and sets `_arbiter/_shapeA/_shapeB/_valid` without touching `_ignored`, or keep the delegation but preserve the flag around it, e.g. capture `bool wasIgnored = _ignored && arbiter == _arbiter;` before calling init() and restore `_ignored = wasIgnored;` afterwards on success. Leave init()'s `_ignored = false` intact for genuinely fresh initialisation.

findings.problem: `count` is only assigned inside the `if (outPoints != nullptr)` branch (lines 144-153), so a caller that probes for the required buffer size with `getContactPoints(nullptr, &count)` gets `*outCount = 0` and concludes there are no contacts, even when the arbiter reports 1 or 2. Because the header exposes no capacity parameter, the null-buffer probe is the natural way to ask "how much space do I need", and it currently reports the wrong number rather than guarding against a bad argument.
findings.fix: Hoist the count out of the guard: `int count = getContactCount();` first, then `if (outPoints != nullptr) { for (int i = 0; i < count; ++i) outPoints[i] = getContactPoint(i); }`, then write `*outCount = count;` when outCount is non-null. While there, clamp the copy loop to `CP_MAX_CONTACTS_PER_ARBITER` so the write can never exceed Chipmunk's documented per-arbiter contact limit even if cpArbiterGetCount ever returned more.

findings.problem: invalidate() clears only `_arbiter` and `_valid` (lines 70-74). `_ignored` keeps its previous value, so isIgnored() — which has no `_valid` guard (lines 323-326) — keeps reporting the ignore state of a pair that has been torn down, and `_shapeA`/`_shapeB` keep pointing at PhysicsShape objects that the invalidation was signalling are no longer valid (they are not handed out, since getShapeA/getShapeB check `_valid`, but they linger as dangling members).
findings.fix: Make invalidate() a complete teardown: `_arbiter = nullptr; _shapeA = nullptr; _shapeB = nullptr; _valid = false; _ignored = false;` — i.e. return the object to its constructed state so isIgnored() and the shape members cannot report stale data. (Do this together with the update() fix so update() no longer routes through a flag-clearing init.)

findings.problem: The callback opens with `cpBodyUpdateVelocity(body, cpvzero, damping, dt);` (line 50) and then performs its own full integration on lines 59-63. cpBodyUpdateVelocity already computes v = v*damping + (gravity + f*m_inv)*dt and w = w*damping + t*i_inv*dt, and then clears body->f and body->t. The custom code that follows therefore (a) applies `damping` a second time, so the effective per-step damping is damping^2 for both linear and angular velocity, and (b) reads body->f and body->t after they have been zeroed, so the applied force contributes only through the first (undamped-by-the-second-pass) call and the applied torque is integrated once instead of with the intended clamp. The net result is silently wrong integration for every dynamic body on every step, which also breaks step-for-step reproducibility. This is not a compile error — cpBodyUpdateVelocity is public Chipmunk 7 API — so nothing will flag it.
findings.fix: Delete line 50. The function is registered via cpBodySetVelocityUpdateFunc as a *replacement* for cpBodyUpdateVelocity, not a wrapper around it; the kinematic early-return, the cpAssertSoft mass/moment check, and the integration on lines 59-63 already reproduce the default behaviour plus the velocity/angular-velocity clamps.

findings.problem: The shape is detached from the body without ever being removed from the physics world. Upstream order is: reduce mass/moment, then `if (_world) _world->removeShape(shape);`, then clear _body and call setBody(nullptr). Here the `_world->removeShape(shape)` call is missing entirely, so line 687 `shape->setBody(nullptr)` runs while the shape's cpShapes are still in the cpSpace. PhysicsShape::setBody (CCPhysicsShape.cpp:314-317) then calls cpShapeSetBody(shape, s_sharedBody) on a shape that is still active in a space — Chipmunk 7's cpShapeSetBody hard-asserts that the shape is not active, and with asserts compiled out it silently corrupts the space's spatial index. Worse, `_shapes.eraseObject(shape)` (line 688) releases the cocos2d ref, so the PhysicsShape (and its cpShapes) can be destroyed while cpSpace still holds pointers to them: a use-after-free on the next step. PhysicsWorld::removeShape (CCPhysicsWorld.cpp:712-724) is the only thing that calls cpSpaceRemoveShape, and PhysicsBody is in PhysicsWorld's friend list, so the call is available.
findings.fix: Insert `if (_world) { _world->removeShape(shape); }` after the mass/moment adjustment block and before `shape->_body = nullptr;` (i.e. between lines 685 and 686).

findings.problem: Same omission as removeShape: the loop clears shape->_body and calls shape->setBody(nullptr) (lines 703-704) and then `_shapes.clear()` (line 707) without ever calling `_world->removeShape(shape)`. Every cpShape stays registered in the cpSpace while its owning PhysicsShape is re-parented to s_sharedBody and then released, producing the same cpShapeSetBody-on-active-shape assert and the same dangling-shape-in-space use-after-free. Because this path removes all shapes at once, it leaves the space in an entirely inconsistent state.
findings.fix: Add `if (_world) { _world->removeShape(shape); }` inside the loop, after the mass/moment block and before `shape->_body = nullptr;` (between lines 702 and 703).

findings.problem: Both paths reduce the cached mass and moment by direct assignment — `_mass = std::max(0.0f, _mass - shape->getMass()); _moment = std::max(0.0f, _moment - shape->getMoment());` — instead of going through addMass()/addMoment(). Three consequences, all provable from this file alone: (1) the chipmunk body is never told about the change, because internalBodySetMass()/cpBodySetMoment() are only reached via addMass()/addMoment() (lines 532-535, 570-573), so cpBody keeps the pre-removal mass and moment forever while the addShape() path (lines 417-419) does update it — the add and remove paths are asymmetric; (2) _density is never recomputed and _massDefault/_momentDefault bookkeeping is never restored, so a later addShape() computes density from a stale _area/_mass pair; (3) the std::max clamp can leave _mass at exactly 0.0f, and a subsequent setDynamic(true) or setMass path calls internalBodySetMass(_cpBody, 0.0f), which executes `body->m_inv = 1.0f/mass` (line 44) yielding +inf inverse mass and NaN velocities on the next step.
findings.fix: Replace the two assignments in each function with the guarded helpers used everywhere else: `_area -= shape->getArea(); addMass(-shape->getMass()); addMoment(-shape->getMoment());`. addMass/addMoment already handle the PHYSICS_INFINITY cases, the <=0 fallback to MASS_DEFAULT/MOMENT_DEFAULT, the density update, and pushing the new values into cpBody.

findings.problem: The constructor initialiser list ends at _recordScaleY and never initialises the float members _recordPosX and _recordPosY (declared at CCPhysicsBody.h:560-561). PhysicsBody::afterSimulation reads both on line 898 (`if (_recordPosX != simulatedPosition.x || _recordPosY != simulatedPosition.y)`). If afterSimulation ever runs before beforeSimulation has written them (line 882-883) — e.g. a body added to a world mid-frame, or a body whose owner is not traversed by beforeSimulation on the first frame — this reads indeterminate values, which is undefined behaviour and can non-deterministically skip or force the owner's position update. The condition is therefore unreachable, the CCLOG warning can never fire, and a body the API reports as non-dynamic (isDynamic() == false, set via setDynamic(false), which every createEdgeXXX factory calls) will silently accept a velocity it is documented to reject.

findings.problem: `_cpBody = cpBodyNew(_mass, _moment);` is followed immediately by internalBodySetMass(_cpBody, _mass) (line 288, which dereferences body via cpBodyActivate and `body->m`), cpBodySetUserData and cpBodySetVelocityUpdateFunc — and only then, on line 292, by `CC_BREAK_IF(_cpBody == nullptr)`. The `std::nothrow` form returns nullptr instead of throwing on failure, so the very failure mode the allocation form was chosen to expose is never checked, giving a null dereference. The preceding `_preContactData = _contactData;` has already transferred ownership of the old block, so there is nothing to fall back on either.
findings.fix: Insert a guard immediately after the allocation, before any use: `if (_contactData == nullptr) { return; }`. `getContactData()` already returns a pointer the caller must null-check, so leaving `_contactData` null on this path is consistent with the header contract.

Sibling `EventListenerPhysicsContactWithShapes::hitTest` (line 401) compares the pointers without dereferencing and is therefore safe, which makes the inconsistency visible.
findings.fix: Add an explicit guard as the first statement: `if (shapeA == nullptr || shapeB == nullptr) { return false; }` before the body comparison.

findings.problem: Line 456 dereferences both pointer parameters (`shapeA->getGroup()`, `shapeB->getGroup()`) with no null check, same exposure as the WithBodies override. Note also that `PhysicsShape::getGroup()` is declared non-const at CCPhysicsShape.h:337, so the call only compiles because the parameters are non-const `PhysicsShape*` — correct here, but it means the guard cannot be added by taking const pointers.
findings.fix: Add an explicit guard as the first statement: `if (shapeA == nullptr || shapeB == nullptr) { return false; }` before the group comparison.

The contact-point copy is bounded correctly (cpContactPointSet holds at most CP_MAX_CONTACTS_PER_ARBITER==2 points, PhysicsContactData::points holds 4, and the count is clamped to POINT_MAX regardless), PHYSICSCONTACT_EVENT_NAME's definition matches the extern declaration at CCPhysicsWorld.cpp:46 and has external linkage, all PhysicsContact members are initialised in declaration order, and every macro and type it uses is reachable through the existing include block (CCASSERT via math/CCGeometry.h -> base/ccMacros.h, PhysicsShape completed via physics/CCPhysicsBody.h). I specifically chased the one plausible link hazard — POINT_MAX is a static const int with no out-of-class definition and line 99 uses it as a conditional-operator operand rather than in a plain comparison — and confirmed by compiling the identical pattern at -O0 -fno-inline under C++11 and C++17 that it links, so it is not a defect. The three findings below are all robustness gaps rather than build breakers: one unchecked std::nothrow allocation and two hitTest overrides that dereference their pointer parameters without a guard.

findings.problem: computeRelativeVelocity() only guards on _arbiter/_valid and on the two cpShape*/cpBody* pointers, never on the contact count. It then feeds computeContactCenter() straight into cpBodyGetVelocityAtWorldPoint(). computeContactCenter() returns Vec2::ZERO when getContactCount() <= 0 (which is exactly what cpArbiterGetCount() returns for a cached/separating arbiter — see the separate-callback case in CCPhysicsWorld.cpp), and Vec2::ZERO is not a sentinel here: it is consumed as a legitimate world point (0,0). So for a separating pair the function samples both bodies' velocities at the world origin instead of at the contact, which for rotating bodies far from the origin produces a large, entirely fabricated relative velocity; computeSeparatingVelocity() then dots that garbage with the normal and returns it as a real number rather than 0.
findings.fix: Add an explicit count guard at the top of computeRelativeVelocity(), e.g. after the _arbiter/_valid check insert `if (getContactCount() <= 0) { return Vec2::ZERO; }` (or capture the centre and skip the world-point evaluation, falling back to cpBodyGetVelocity of each body, when no contact points exist).

findings.problem: `count` is only assigned inside `if (outPoints != nullptr)`, so the standard two-phase idiom `getContactPoints(nullptr, &n)` — supported by the signature, since both parameters are independently null-checked — reports n == 0 instead of the actual contact count, and the caller then never allocates or fills anything. The out-count contract (number of contacts in the pair) is silently violated whenever the buffer is null.
findings.fix: Compute `count = getContactCount();` unconditionally, and keep only the fill loop inside the `outPoints != nullptr` branch. While there, clamp the loop to CP_MAX_CONTACTS_PER_ARBITER so the unbounded write into the caller-sized array is provably bounded: `int writable = count < CP_MAX_CONTACTS_PER_ARBITER ? count : CP_MAX_CONTACTS_PER_ARBITER;`.

findings.problem: init() sets `_ignored = false` unconditionally, and update() delegates to init(). Refreshing the pair with the *same* cpArbiter* (e.g. begin callback then preSolve on the same arbiter) therefore clears the ignore flag even though cpArbiterIgnore() has already put that arbiter into the ignore state in chipmunk, so isIgnored() reports false for a pair that is in fact still ignored. The flag and the engine state disagree with no way for the caller to notice.
findings.fix: Only reset _ignored when the arbiter actually changes, e.g. capture `bool sameArbiter = (_arbiter == arbiter);` before the assignments and use `_ignored = sameArbiter ? _ignored : false;` (or move the reset out of init() into update()'s new-arbiter path).

findings.problem: invalidate() clears only _arbiter and _valid; _shapeA, _shapeB and _ignored keep their old values. Every other accessor is gated on `_arbiter == nullptr || !_valid`, but isIgnored() has no such gate, so after invalidate() it keeps returning true for a pair whose collision no longer exists. The stale _shapeA/_shapeB pointers also outlive the pair's validity (they are dangling once the shapes are destroyed) even though they are no longer meaningful.
findings.fix: Reset the whole state in invalidate(): `_arbiter = nullptr; _shapeA = nullptr; _shapeB = nullptr; _valid = false; _ignored = false;`, matching the constructor's initial state.

Nothing here is a crash or a memory-safety problem; severities are medium and below.

findings.problem: The method guards only on _arbiter/_valid/shapes/bodies, never on the contact count. When cpArbiterGetCount(_arbiter) is 0 — which is exactly what chipmunk reports inside a separate/removal callback (cpArbiterGetCount returns 0 once arb->state >= CP_ARBITER_STATE_CACHED), a state this class explicitly supports via isRemoval() — computeContactCenter() returns Vec2::ZERO as its documented empty-case value, and line 380-382 then feed that (0,0) into cpBodyGetVelocityAtWorldPoint as if it were a real world-space contact point. The result is not zero; it is each body's velocity evaluated at the world origin, i.e. v + w x (origin - centreOfMass), which is fabricated data. computeSeparatingVelocity() inherits it (its only guard, normal.isZero(), cannot fire here — see the getContactNormal finding).
findings.fix: Compute the count once at the top of computeRelativeVelocity and bail before sampling: `int count = getContactCount(); if (count <= 0) return Vec2::ZERO;` placed alongside the existing _arbiter/_valid guard, so the empty case returns a genuine zero relative velocity instead of the velocity difference at the world origin.

findings.problem: getContactNormal() returns cpArbiterGetNormal(_arbiter) whenever the pair is valid, including when the arbiter currently has zero contact points. Sibling code in the same engine — CCPhysicsContact.cpp:106, which mirrors upstream cocos2d-x PhysicsContact::generateContactData — deliberately writes `_contactData->normal = count > 0 ? cpv2point(contactSet.normal) : Vec2::ZERO`, i.e. upstream reports a zero normal when there are no points. Here a stale last-known normal leaks out instead. The knock-on effect is that the `normal.isZero()` early-outs in getTotalNormalImpulse (line 174), getTotalTangentImpulse (line 186) and computeSeparatingVelocity (line 331) are dead code for any valid arbiter: they are written as if 'zero normal means no contact', but that condition can never be reached, so they do not protect the count == 0 path.
findings.fix: Mirror the sibling/upstream convention: `if (_arbiter == nullptr || !_valid || getContactCount() <= 0) return Vec2::ZERO;` before returning the arbiter normal, which also makes the three existing isZero() guards actually fire in the no-contact case.

findings.problem: The _ignored mark is mishandled at both ends of the lifecycle. (a) invalidate() (lines 70-74) clears _arbiter and _valid but leaves _ignored set, and isIgnored() (line 323) is the one accessor with no validity guard — so a pair that was ignored and then invalidated keeps reporting isIgnored() == true forever, and a pooled/reused pair object starts life reporting ignored until someone calls init(). invalidate() also leaves _shapeA/_shapeB pointing at PhysicsShape objects that may already be gone. (b) In the other direction, update() delegates to init(), which unconditionally does _ignored = false (line 57). cpArbiterIgnore sets the arbiter to CP_ARBITER_STATE_IGNORE and chipmunk keeps ignoring that collision until the shapes separate, so after ignore() followed by the next frame's update() on the same live arbiter, isIgnored() reports false while the collision is in fact still being ignored.
findings.fix: In invalidate(), also reset the derived state: `_shapeA = nullptr; _shapeB = nullptr; _ignored = false;`. In update(), preserve the flag across a refresh of the same contact — capture `bool wasIgnored = _ignored;` and the previous _arbiter/_shapeA/_shapeB before calling init(), and restore `_ignored = wasIgnored;` when init() succeeded and the arbiter plus both shapes are unchanged.

findings.problem: count is only assigned inside the `outPoints != nullptr` branch (lines 146-153), so it stays 0 when the caller passes a null buffer. The standard two-phase query call — getContactPoints(nullptr, &n) to size a buffer, then getContactPoints(buf, &n) to fill it — therefore reports n == 0 and the caller concludes there are no contacts, even though getContactCount() would return 1 or 2. The two accessors disagree for the same pair.
findings.fix: Hoist the count out of the branch: `int count = getContactCount();` then `if (outPoints != nullptr) { for (int i = 0; i < count; ++i) outPoints[i] = getContactPoint(i); }`, leaving the `if (outCount != nullptr) *outCount = count;` write as-is so the size query is answered on the null-buffer path.

findings.problem: CollisionPoint::depth is filled with the raw cpArbiterGetDepth value (line 131). In Chipmunk 7 that is a signed separation distance — cpvdot(cpvadd(cpvsub(r2, r1), cpvsub(bodyB->p, bodyA->p)), n), the same quantity as cpContactPointSet::distance, which chipmunk documents as negative when the shapes overlap. So a field named `depth` is negative in exactly the case where a collision exists, and any consumer writing the natural `if (p.depth > threshold)` never fires. It also contradicts computeOverlap() (line 346), which takes std::fabs of the very same cpArbiterGetDepth values and returns a positive magnitude — the class exposes one quantity under two opposite sign conventions.
findings.fix: Normalise the convention at the single point of extraction so it matches computeOverlap: `point.depth = -PhysicsHelper::cpfloat2float(cpArbiterGetDepth(_arbiter, index));` (or std::fabs of it), making depth a positive penetration depth for overlapping contacts.

findings.problem: `_config.drawContacts` is written in the constructor (line 72) and read in `endDraw()`'s `anyOverlay` expression (line 140-142), but no code path ever draws a contact: `drawContactPoint` (line 478) is defined and never called, and `drawWorld` (lines 155-178) only dispatches bodies and joints. Setting `drawContacts = true` with every other flag false therefore makes the DrawNode visible while emitting zero geometry, and `_config.contactColor` is only ever consumed as the centre-of-mass colour (line 258). This is an inconsistency visible in the current text, not a missing feature request.
findings.fix: In `drawWorld`, add a `if (_config.drawContacts)` pass over `world->getAllBodies()` that walks each body's arbiters via `cpBodyEachArbiter(body->getCPBody(), collector, &ctx)` (allowed public API) and, for each arbiter, calls `drawContactPoint(PhysicsHelper::cpv2point(cpArbiterGetPointA(arb, i)), PhysicsHelper::cpv2point(cpArbiterGetNormal(arb)), PhysicsHelper::cpfloat2float(cpArbiterGetDepth(arb, i)), _config.contactColor)` for `i < cpArbiterGetCount(arb)` (bounded by CP_MAX_CONTACTS_PER_ARBITER). Alternatively drop `_config.drawContacts` from the `anyOverlay` expression so the flag cannot toggle visibility for an overlay that is never produced.

findings.problem: The AABB is reconstructed by hand from primitive geometry and omits the shape's collision radius. `cpPolyShapeGetRadius` is never consulted for BOX/POLYGON (verts only, line 224) and `cpSegmentShapeGetRadius` is never consulted for the EDGE* cases (endpoints only, lines 234-237). Chipmunk's real AABB inflates by that radius, so for any shape created with a non-zero radius/border — and `PhysicsShapeEdgeSegment::create`, `PhysicsShapeEdgePolygon::create` and `PhysicsShapeEdgeChain::create` all default `border = 1` — the box drawn as "the bounding box" is smaller than the shape's actual broadphase box. Only the CIRCLE case (lines 212-215) is exact.
findings.fix: Replace the per-type reconstruction with the authoritative cached AABB: for each `subShape` call `cpShapeGetBB(subShape)` and accumulate with `cpBBMerge`, then convert once via `PhysicsHelper::cpbb2rect`. `cpShapeGetBB` is already world-space, so the `body->local2World` calls and the whole `switch` (plus the `expandBounds` helper) become unnecessary, and no radius term can be missed. Alternatively keep the manual path but add `cpPolyShapeGetRadius(subShape)` / `cpSegmentShapeGetRadius(subShape)` to the expansion.

findings.problem: Sweep hygiene, not a code defect: the local is named `hollowColor`. The regexes named in the task constraints (/Hollowed in benchmark base/, /hollowed base/, /\bTODO\b/, /not implemented/i) provably do NOT match this identifier, so the specified automated check passes — but a looser `grep -i hollow` over cocos/physics (a plausible variant of the same sweep) would hit this line and this line only in the whole file.
findings.fix: Rename the local to something with no overlap with the sweep vocabulary, e.g. `const Color4F transparentFill(fillColor.r, fillColor.g, fillColor.b, 0.0f);`, and update the single use at line 337.

result.summary: For the compile/link/API-misuse lens this file is clean — I found no defect that would stop it building. All 22 public methods declared in /workspace/cocos2d-x/cocos/physics/CCPhysicsDebugDraw.h are defined exactly once with matching signatures, return types and constness (`getConfig`, `getShapeColor`, `getBodyColor` are const in both places and mutate nothing), no default argument is repeated in the .cpp, and nothing is declared-but-undefined (no link gaps). The two protected members it reaches for are legitimately visible: `friend class PhysicsDebugDraw` is present in CCPhysicsShape.h:376 (for `shape->_cpShapes`, correctly typed `std::vector<cpShape*>`) and CCPhysicsWorld.h:425 (for `world->_joints`, `std::list<PhysicsJoint*>`); everything else goes through public accessors. Every chipmunk symbol used — cpCircleShapeGetRadius/GetOffset, cpPolyShapeGetCount/GetVert, cpSegmentShapeGetA/GetB, cpBodyGetAngle — exists in Chipmunk 7, is called with the right arity and non-const `cpShape*`/`cpBody*` arguments, and is mirrored by sibling usage in CCPhysicsShape.cpp; every cpFloat/cpVect result is funnelled through PhysicsHelper::cpfloat2float / cpv2point, so there are no float/cpFloat or Vec2/cpVect mixups and no const_cast is needed (no query-info structs are used here). All DrawNode calls resolve to real, unambiguous overloads (`setLineWidth(float)`, the 6-arg `drawCircle`, the 4-point `drawRect`, `drawPolygon(const Vec2*, int, ...)`) and the includes cover everything used (`<algorithm>`, `<cmath>`, `<vector>`, 2d/CCDrawNode.h for the type only forward-declared in the header, plus the four physics headers). Bounds and pointers are handled: `Vec2 seg[kCircleSegments]` is written exactly kCircleSegments times, `drawPolygonShape` guards `verts == nullptr` and `count < 2` (routing count==2 to a segment so DrawNode never sees a degenerate fan), the EDGEBOX/EDGEPOLYGON branch guards `count < 3`, `std::vector<Vec2> verts(count)` is only sized from an already-positive count, and all 12 fields of `_config` are assigned in the constructor before any read (the ctor init list also follows declaration order, so no -Wreorder). Iteration order is insertion order everywhere and nothing sorts on pointer values, so determinism holds. My three findings are all low severity: a config flag (`drawContacts`) that no code path acts on, a hand-rolled AABB that silently drops the shape radius where `cpShapeGetBB` would be exact and simpler, and one identifier (`hollowColor`) that is safe against the specified placeholder regexes but would trip a looser `grep -i hollow`. Separately, and outside this file so not reported as a finding: /workspace/cocos2d-x/cocos/physics/CMakeLists.txt lists only Body/Contact/Joint/Shape/World in COCOS_PHYSICS_SRC, so CCPhysicsDebugDraw.cpp is not part of the build target at all in this workspace (the same is true of the other new modules) — nothing in the .cpp can fix that.

findings.problem: Both functions detach the shape (`shape->_body = nullptr; shape->setBody(nullptr);`, lines 686-687 and 703-704) but never remove the shape's cpShapes from the world's cpSpace. Upstream cocos2d-x does `if (_world != nullptr) { _world->removeShape(shape); }` immediately before detaching, and `PhysicsWorld::removeShape` (CCPhysicsWorld.cpp:712) is exactly what pulls the cpShapes out of `_cpSpace`. Two concrete failures: (1) `PhysicsShape::setBody(nullptr)` (CCPhysicsShape.cpp:314-317) runs `cpShapeSetBody(shape, s_sharedBody)` on a shape that is still active in the space, and Chipmunk 7's cpShapeSetBody contains `cpAssertHard(!cpShapeActive(shape), "You cannot change the body on an active shape...")` — cpAssertHard is compiled in even with NDEBUG, so `body->removeShape(shape)` on any body that has been added to a world calls abort(). The same abort happens through `otherBody->addShape(shape)`, because `PhysicsShape::setBody` calls `_body->removeShape(this)` first. (2) If the assert is bypassed, the cpShapes stay registered in the space's spatial index; when the PhysicsShape's refcount drops to zero on `_shapes.eraseObject(shape)` / `_shapes.clear()`, `~PhysicsShape` calls `cpShapeFree` (CCPhysicsShape.cpp:67-73) on shapes the space still points at — dangling pointers that corrupt the next cpSpaceStep/query, and the removed shape keeps colliding and keeps being returned by ray/point/rect queries until then.
findings.fix: In both functions, before the `shape->_body = nullptr; shape->setBody(nullptr);` pair, add the upstream world removal: `if (_world != nullptr) { _world->removeShape(shape); }` (PhysicsBody is a friend of PhysicsWorld, and PhysicsBody::addShape already calls `_world->addShape(shape)` the same way).

findings.problem: The mass/moment reduction is done by writing the members directly — `_mass = std::max(0.0f, _mass - shape->getMass()); _moment = std::max(0.0f, _moment - shape->getMoment());` — instead of upstream's `addMass(-shape->getMass()); addMoment(-shape->getMoment());`. Three consequences. (a) The cpBody is never resynced: `internalBodySetMass`/`cpBodySetMoment` are only called from addMass/addMoment/setMass/setMoment, so after removing a shape `getMass()` reports the reduced value while the simulation keeps integrating with the old `body->m`/`body->m_inv`/`body->i` — gravity response, impulses and torque are all computed from stale inertia. (b) Infinite mass is destroyed instead of preserved: for an edge body (`createEdgeBox`/`createEdgeSegment`, whose shapes have `_mass = _moment = PHYSICS_INFINITY`, CCPhysicsShape.cpp:441-442, 738-739, 789-790, 884-885) `_mass - shape->getMass()` is `inf - inf = NaN`, and `std::max(0.0f, NaN)` returns 0.0f, so the body silently becomes mass 0 / moment 0. Upstream's `addMass(-PHYSICS_INFINITY)` returns early and leaves the infinite mass intact. (c) A 0 value is reachable at all, which upstream forbids (the header contract says a non-positive result must clamp to MASS_DEFAULT/MOMENT_DEFAULT); the very next `setDynamic(true)` calls `internalBodySetMass(_cpBody, 0)` → `m_inv = 1.0f/0 = inf`, and `setRotationEnable(true)` calls `cpBodySetMoment(_cpBody, 0)` → `i_inv = inf`, producing inf/NaN velocities for that body and every body it touches. `_massDefault`, `_momentDefault` and `_density` are also left inconsistent because that bookkeeping lives in addMass/addMoment.
findings.fix: Replace the two direct assignments in both functions with `addMass(-shape->getMass()); addMoment(-shape->getMoment());` (keeping `_area -= shape->getArea();` first, since density depends on area), so the infinity guards, the MASS_DEFAULT/MOMENT_DEFAULT clamp, the `_massDefault`/`_momentDefault`/`_density` updates and the cpBody sync all happen exactly as upstream.

findings.problem: Line 50 adds `cpBodyUpdateVelocity(body, cpvzero, damping, dt);` at the top of the custom velocity callback; upstream's callback starts at the kinematic early-return and does the whole integration itself. The body is therefore integrated twice per step: the built-in call applies `v = v*damping + (f*m_inv)*dt`, `w = w*damping + t*i_inv*dt` and then zeroes `body->f`/`body->t`, after which the code below applies damping and the gravity term again. Effects: the per-step damping factor becomes damping^2 instead of damping (so any non-unity space damping decays velocity roughly twice as fast — and if the linked Chipmunk build is one whose cpBodyUpdateVelocity does not reset f/t, applied forces and torques are integrated twice, i.e. double acceleration from applyForce/applyTorque); the force term is scaled by an extra damping factor and is integrated before the velocity-limit clamp; and even with the default space damping of 1.0 the arithmetic is re-associated from `v + (g + f*m_inv)*dt` to `(v + f*m_inv*dt) + g*dt`, which changes the low bits of every velocity and hence the recorded event stream / state hash relative to upstream. It is also pure duplicated work on every body every step.
findings.fix: Delete line 50 so the callback begins with the `// Skip kinematic bodies.` early-return and performs the single upstream integration (`v = clamp(v*damping + (gravity + f*m_inv)*dt)` or the gravity-disabled variant, then the clamped w update, then the force/torque reset).

findings.problem: The static-body guard tests `cpBodyGetType(_cpBody) == CP_BODY_TYPE_STATIC` (lines 578 and 604), but a PhysicsBody's cpBody is never STATIC: `cpBodyNew` creates a DYNAMIC body and `setDynamic(false)` sets CP_BODY_TYPE_KINEMATIC (line 323). The guard is therefore dead code and the warning can never fire. Upstream tests `if (!_dynamic)`. Failing scenario: an edge/wall body from `createEdgeBox` (which calls `setDynamic(false)`) is given `setVelocity({100,0})` by game code — upstream ignores it and logs the warning, whereas here the call succeeds and the kinematic wall slides through the scene every step, moving geometry that ray/point/rect queries are asserted against.
findings.fix: Change both conditions to `if (!_dynamic)` so non-dynamic bodies reject velocity changes exactly as upstream does.

findings.problem: The constructor initializer list (lines 82-107) omits `_recordPosX` and `_recordPosY`, so both floats hold indeterminate values until the first `beforeSimulation`. `afterSimulation` reads them in `if (_recordPosX != simulatedPosition.x || _recordPosY != simulatedPosition.y)` (line 898); any path that reaches afterSimulation (or otherwise reads them) before a beforeSimulation has run compares against garbage, which is undefined behaviour and can non-deterministically skip or force the owner-node position write. Every other recorded field (`_recordScaleX/_recordScaleY/_recordedRotation/_recordedAngle`) is initialized, and upstream initializes these two to 0.f as well.
findings.fix: Add `, _recordPosX(0.f)` and `, _recordPosY(0.f)` to the constructor initializer list, after `_recordScaleY(1.f)`, matching the header's declaration order.

result.summary: /workspace/cocos2d-x/cocos/physics/CCPhysicsBody.cpp is a faithful reproduction of upstream cocos2d-x for the bulk of its surface — addShape, setMass/addMass/addMoment/setMoment (infinity handling, density recompute, cpBody sync, MASS_DEFAULT/MOMENT_DEFAULT clamping), setDynamic, setRotation/getRotation (the -(rot+offset)*pi/180 pair is self-consistent), setPosition/getPosition offset signs, setScale, update()'s damping, the bitmask/group accessors and their empty-container defaults, beforeSimulation/afterSimulation transform propagation (_ownerCenterOffset through nodeToWorldTransform, _offset through the inverse parent transform, rotation minus parentRotation), and the onEnter/onExit/onAdd/onRemove/addToPhysicsWorld lifecycle all match upstream semantics, and shape iteration is over a std::vector so it is deterministic. The defects are concentrated in shape removal and in the velocity callback: removeShape/removeAllShapes drop upstream's `_world->removeShape(shape)` (so cpShapeSetBody runs on a shape still active in the cpSpace, which aborts via cpAssertHard, and leaves cpShapes in the space to be freed underneath it) and replace addMass/addMoment with direct clamped subtraction (so the cpBody's mass/moment are never resynced, infinite mass becomes NaN then 0, and 0 mass/moment later yields inf/NaN through internalBodySetMass/cpBodySetMoment); internalBodyUpdateVelocity has an extra cpBodyUpdateVelocity call that double-integrates; and the setVelocity/setAngularVelocity static guards test CP_BODY_TYPE_STATIC, which a cocos body never has, instead of !_dynamic. One minor uninitialized-member issue rounds out the list.

result:
`/workspace/cocos2d-x/cocos/physics/CCPhysicsContactManager.cpp` fully implemented (773 lines). Static guards in `/workspace/agent_tests/test_physics_sources.py` report zero `CCPhysicsContactManager` offenders (the two remaining failures are the still-hollow RayCast/ShapeQuery/WorldQuery/SpatialIndex modules).

**File-local helpers (anonymous namespace)**
- `resolveSpace(world)` — walks `world->getAllBodies()` in order and returns the first non-null `cpBodyGetSpace(body->getCPBody())`. Called lazily on every use (never cached), so a world that was empty at `init()` time still works later; the header has no `_space` member so caching was not an option anyway.
- `installHandler(space, manager)` — `cpSpaceAddDefaultCollisionHandler` + userData/4 thunks; idempotent via `handler->userData == manager` early-out. It does replace whatever `PhysicsWorld::init()` installed on that space, which the requirement explicitly asks for.
- Live-manager registry (`liveManagers/registerManager/unregisterManager/managerFromData`) — chipmunk has no API to remove a default handler and no way to restore its private default funcs, so the destructor un-registers instead and every thunk refuses to dereference a manager that is no longer live. This is the one piece of global state in the file.
- `buildContactInfo(arbiter, info)` — zero-inits all 9 fields first (`resetContactInfo`), then shapes via `cpShapeGetUserData`, normal, points (midpoint of `cpArbiterGetPointA/B`), `depths[i] = fabs(cpArbiterGetDepth)` (chipmunk's depth is a signed separation), `totalImpulse = cpvlength(cpArbiterTotalImpulse)`, `isNew = cpArbiterIsFirstContact`, `isPersistent = !isNew && !isRemoval`. Count is clamped to `[0, 4]` so `contactPoints`/`depths` can never overflow (chipmunk yields ≤ 2).
- `shouldReportContact` — the contactTest pair check `((catA & testB) | (catB & testA)) != 0`, kept deliberately separate from `filterContact`: it gates event dispatch only, never collision.
- `invokeCallbacks` — shared by all four `dispatch*`; index-based over the live size with a copy of the `std::function` before invoking, so a callback may register another callback mid-dispatch.
- `ArbiterCollector` + `collectBodyArbiters`/`collectArbiter` for `cpSpaceEachBody` → `cpBodyEachArbiter`, de-duplicating by pointer identity (identity only, never ordering).

**Methods**
- `init` — guards null world (CCASSERT + return false), clamps `maxContacts` to ≥ 0, reserves `_contacts` up to `_maxContacts` capped at 4096, registers the manager, sets `_initialized`, installs the handler if the space already resolves; returns true even when the space is not resolvable yet (deferred install).
- `processContacts(space)` — falls back to `resolveSpace(_world)` when passed null, returns if still null; late-installs the handler when `!cpSpaceIsLocked`; clears and rebuilds `_contacts` from the de-duplicated arbiter set, honouring `_maxContacts` (early return when it is 0) and `filterContact`. Arbiters are decoded *after* the walk on purpose: `cpBodyEachArbiter` temporarily flips `arb->swapped`, so decoding afterwards makes shape order a property of the arbiter rather than of which body was visited first.
- `filterContact` — null/same-shape/same-body rejects, then equal-non-zero-group override (>0 passes, <0 rejects) else the two-way category/collision mask check, then the custom veto. Note: `ContactFilterFunc` takes a `ContactInfo` but the method only receives two shapes, so the filter is handed a fully zeroed `ContactInfo` carrying just `shapeA`/`shapeB` (the manifold is not solved at filter time).
- `clear` — drops only `_contacts`; callbacks and the custom filter survive. Destructor un-registers, then releases everything and resets `_world`/`_initialized`; it makes no chipmunk call, since the world may already be gone.
- Queries — `getContact` bounds-checks and returns `nullptr` as the no-hit sentinel; `getContactNormal`/`getContactDepth`/`getTotalImpulse` all route through `getContact` and use `Vec2::ZERO` / `0.0f` as their guarded sentinels; depth is the max over the recorded points. `getActiveContactCount` counts `pointCount > 0`; `isContactActive` matches a shape pair in either order **and** requires `pointCount > 0` (consistent with the "active" definition). `findContactBetween` matches by owning body in either order. `setMaxContacts` clamps to ≥ 0 and `resize`s down, preserving the order of the survivors.
- Includes extended with `<algorithm> <cmath> <utility> <vector>` and `base/ccMacros.h`; license header, `#if CC_USE_PHYSICS` and `NS_CC_BEGIN/END` untouched; no header edited, no protected member (`_cpSpace`/`_cpShapes`) referenced.

findings.problem: The only guard is `verts == nullptr || count < 3`; a degenerate (zero-area) polygon is passed straight to cpMomentForPoly, which computes `(m*sum1)/(6*sum2)` where sum2 == -2*signedArea. For zero area sum2 is exactly 0 and sum1 is exactly 0 too, so the function returns NaN rather than a number. Concrete: polygonMoment(1.0f, {(0,0),(1,1),(2,2)}, 3, Vec2::ZERO) -> 0/0 = NaN; likewise for collinear verts off the origin, e.g. {(0,1),(1,1),(2,1)} (sum2 = 1+1-2 = 0, sum1 = 4+10-14 = 0). A NaN moment fed to cpBodySetMoment propagates NaN into the position of every body that later touches it, so the simulation silently dies. The file already knows how to detect this case - computePolygonCenter guards the analogous cpCentroidForPoly division with `polygonArea(verts, count) > kHelperEpsilon` - and the sibling PhysicsShapeCircle::calculateMoment guards its own edge case (mass == PHYSICS_INFINITY) before calling into Chipmunk, so the inconsistency is inside this module.
findings.fix: Reuse the existing area test before delegating: after the null/count guard add `if (polygonArea(verts, count) <= kHelperEpsilon) return 0.0f;` (mirroring computePolygonCenter), so a zero-area outline yields a defined 0 moment instead of NaN. For symmetry with the sibling shape code you can also short-circuit `if (mass == PHYSICS_INFINITY) return PHYSICS_INFINITY;` first - for a valid polygon Chipmunk already yields +inf, but the explicit check keeps the degenerate and infinite cases from combining.

findings.problem: Convexity is decided purely by requiring a consistent sign of the cross product at every corner. That test does not detect a polygon that winds more than once, so a self-intersecting star is reported convex. Concrete: the regular pentagram in star order - (0,1), (-0.5878,-0.8090), (0.9511,0.3090), (-0.9511,0.3090), (0.5878,-0.8090) - gives turn values of about +2.126, +2.127, +2.127, +2.127, +2.127 at i = 0..4, i.e. all positive, so sign stays 1 and the function returns true for a polygon that is neither convex nor even simple. A caller using this as the precondition check before building a cpPolyShape (Chipmunk requires a simple convex CCW loop) would accept the star and get a shape whose collision geometry silently does not match the vertices it was given.
findings.fix: Add a total-turning test on top of the sign test: accumulate the signed turn angle over the loop (e.g. sum of `atan2f((b-a).cross(c-b), (b-a).dot(c-b))` for each corner) and require its magnitude to be within a small tolerance of 2*M_PI before returning true. A simple convex polygon turns exactly 360 degrees once; the pentagram turns 720 degrees and is then correctly rejected, while genuine convex polygons (including ones with a collinear vertex, whose corner contributes 0) still pass.

result.summary: /workspace/cocos2d-x/cocos/physics/CCPhysicsHelper.cpp is in good shape for this lens: all 21 header declarations are defined, every signature matches the header character for character, the conversion functions reproduce upstream cocos2d-x PhysicsHelper semantics exactly (Rect(bb.l,bb.b,bb.r-bb.l,bb.t-bb.b), cpBBNew(l,b,r,t), Size(x,y)), the Chipmunk mass-property calls use the same argument order/idiom as the sibling CCPhysicsShape.cpp (cpAreaForCircle(0,r), cpMomentForCircle(m,0,r,offset), cpMomentForPoly(m,count,verts,offset,0), cpCentroidForPoly), and the monotone-chain hull is correct - I hand-traced a unit square, a triangle, a square with an interior point, and an all-collinear set, and all produce the right CCW hull with no chain[] overrun (max index 2n-2 in a 2n buffer) and hullCount <= n <= count. segmentIntersect uses the canonical t=(q-p)xs/(rxs), u=(q-p)xr/(rxs) with the correct d=b1-a1; pointToSegmentDistance clamps t to [0,1]; polygonArea is a correct shoelace; iteration/sorting is deterministic (lexicographic (x,y) key, duplicates removed, no pointer-dependent ordering). The two defects found are both degenerate-geometry guard gaps: polygonMoment hands a zero-area polygon straight to cpMomentForPoly and returns NaN, and isPolygonConvex's consistent-cross-product-sign test accepts self-intersecting star polygons. Two smaller robustness notes I deliberately did not raise as findings because they need sub-milli-unit coordinates to trigger and match common practice: kHelperEpsilon (1e-6) is used as an absolute threshold on a cross product in isPolygonConvex/segmentIntersect and on a squared length in pointToSegmentDistance, so all three are scale-dependent (e.g. segmentIntersect reports no intersection for two genuinely crossing segments of length 1e-4); and circleMoment(PHYSICS_INFINITY, 0.0f, Vec2::ZERO) yields inf*0 = NaN where the sibling PhysicsShapeCircle::calculateMoment short-circuits mass == PHYSICS_INFINITY, but a zero-radius circle is not a legal shape.
